note: Pick the case (stage 6, extended in A2 extras); w or na? (A1 extras); the going tree with chodzić / jeździć and pójść / pojechać and Imperfective or perfective? (A2 extras). B1 adds the prefixed verbs of motion to the going tree.

trees.title: Pick the case
trees.intro: Think of one noun in your sentence and answer the questions about it.

start.question: Is there a preposition right before the noun (or before its adjective)?
start.help: Prepositions are short words such as do, z, w, na, bez, dla, u.

options.label: Yes, there is a preposition
No preposition
do, od, bez, dla, u, obok, koło, naprzeciwko, blisko, niedaleko
options.why: These prepositions always take the genitive.

options.label: z
na
w
przez, or za meaning in … time or for (za tydzień, dziękuję za pomoc)
options.why: przez and za meaning in … time or for take the accusative: Wracam za tydzień. Dziękuję za pomoc. (za meaning behind takes the instrumental: za domem.)

example.en: I'm coming back in a week.

options.label: o, po, przy (about, after, next to)
options.why: o, po and przy usually take the locative: mówić o filmie, po lekcji, przy oknie. (o meaning for, as in prosić o, takes the accusative, and so does po meaning to fetch: Idę po chleb.)

options.label: przed, za (behind), pod, nad, między (in front of, behind, under, above, between)
options.why: When they say where something is, these prepositions take the instrumental: przed domem, za kościołem, pod łóżkiem, nad morzem. Going there takes the accusative: Jedziemy nad morze, Kot wchodzi pod stół.

example.en: I'm waiting in front of the house.

options.label: from, out of (Where from?)
options.why: z meaning from takes the genitive.

options.label: with, together with (With whom? With what?)
options.why: z meaning with takes the instrumental.

na.question: Does na say where something goes, or where it is?

options.label: Where it goes (Where to?)
options.why: na + accusative = where to.

options.label: Where it is (Where?)
options.why: na + locative = where.

options.label: Where something is (Where?)
options.why: w + locative = where: in a building, a town, a country.

options.label: Where someone goes: into a building, a town, a country
options.why: Going into a place usually takes do + genitive, not w: Idę do szkoły, not Idę w szkołę.

options.label: A day of the week (on Monday …)
options.why: w + a day of the week takes the accusative. (Months and years take the locative: w maju.)

options.label: A month or a year (in May, in 2025)
options.why: w + a month or a year takes the locative.

example.en: I have a holiday in May.

role.question: What does the noun do in the sentence?

options.label: It is the subject: the person or thing that does the action
options.why: The subject is in the nominative. (After quantity words like dużo or pięć it goes into the genitive: Pięć osób czeka.)

options.label: It comes after to jest or to są
options.why: After to jest / to są the noun stays in the nominative.

options.label: It is a noun after być saying who someone is (a job, a nationality, a role)
options.why: być + noun takes the instrumental: Jestem lekarzem. With a first name in an introduction the nominative is usual: Jestem Tomek. An adjective after być stays in the nominative: Kawa jest gorąca.

options.label: It is the object of the verb: the person or thing the action goes to
It says whose something is, or follows a quantity word (dużo, mało, pięć …)
options.why: Possession and quantities take the genitive.

example.en: I have a lot of work.

options.label: It is the person who receives something (To whom?)
options.why: The receiver of a gift, a message or help is in the dative.

options.label: It goes with pomagać, dziękować, podobać się, pasować or jest … zimno (the person who is helped, thanked, likes it, is suited or feels it)
options.why: These verbs and phrases take the person in the dative: Pomagam bratu. Dziękuję panu. Podoba mi się. Pasuje ci. Jest mi zimno.

example.pl: Ten film bardzo mi się podoba.

options.label: It is a tool or a means of transport (With what? By what?)
options.why: Tools and means of transport without a preposition take the instrumental.

options.label: You are speaking to someone directly
options.why: Addressing someone takes the vocative.

object.question: Which kind of verb is it?
object.help: A few verbs take another case for their object. Check them first.

options.label: szukać, słuchać, potrzebować, używać, bać się, uczyć się
options.why: These verbs take the genitive, also in a positive sentence: Szukam klucza. Uczę się polskiego.

options.label: pomagać, dziękować, or the person after dawać (komu?)
options.why: The person you help, thank or give something to is in the dative, also after nie. The thing you give stays in the accusative: Daję mamie kwiaty.

options.label: interesować się (be interested in)
options.why: interesować się takes the instrumental: Interesuję się sportem.

options.label: Another verb (mieć, lubić, kupować, czytać …)

negation.question: Is the verb negated with nie?

options.label: Yes, there is nie before the verb
options.why: After nie the direct object switches from the accusative to the genitive.

options.label: No, the sentence is positive
options.why: Most verbs take a direct object in the accusative.

example.en: I'm buying a newspaper and coffee.

trees.title: w or na?
trees.intro: For a place: which little word do you need, and which case follows it?

start.question: What kind of place is it?

options.label: Most buildings, rooms and shops: sklep, bank, szkoła, kino, kuchnia

answer.title: w
answer.text: Most buildings and rooms take w. Where you are: w + locative. Where you go: do + genitive.

options.label: A town, a city or a country

answer.title: w
answer.text: Towns and most countries take w. Where you are: w + locative. Where you go: do + genitive.

options.label: Home

answer.title: w domu / do domu
answer.text: dom takes -u in both: w domu (at home), do domu (home, when you go there).

options.label: A na-place (poczta, dworzec, lotnisko, uniwersytet), a stop, a square, a street, a surface or an event
poczta, dworzec, przystanek, rynek, lotnisko, uniwersytet

answer.title: na
answer.text: These places take na. Learn them as a list. Where you are: na + locative. Where you go: na + accusative.

options.label: An event or a meal: a concert, a lesson, a coffee

answer.title: na
answer.text: Events take na. Where you are: na + locative. Where you go: na + accusative.

options.label: A surface or a street: a table, a shelf, a street

answer.title: na
answer.text: On a surface or in a street: na + locative.

examples.en: The phone is on the table.
The car is in the street.

trees.title: Which verb of going?
trees.intro: English "go" (and "fly") is nine verbs in Polish at A2: iść, jechać, lecieć for one trip, chodzić, jeździć, latać for a habit, and pójść, pojechać, polecieć for one finished trip. Answer two or three questions. (Verbs like przyjść and wyjść come at B1.)

start.question: Is it one trip, or something regular?

options.label: One trip, in one direction
A habit or a repeated trip (codziennie, często, w soboty), or moving in general (walking, cycling, flying as an activity)

when.question: How does the sentence look at the trip?

options.label: Now or planned (Teraz idę…, Jutro lecę…), or "was going" in the past while something else happened
As one whole trip that happened or will happen: went, has gone, will go
On foot, or to an everyday place in town when the sentence names no vehicle

answer.title: iść
answer.text: One trip on foot: iść (idę, idziesz, idą). Past "was going": szedłem / szłam.

examples.pl: Teraz idę do sklepu, zaraz wracam.
examples.en: I'm going to the shop now, I'll be right back.

examples.pl: Kiedy szedłem do domu, zaczął padać deszcz.
examples.en: While I was walking home, it started to rain.

options.label: By car, bus, tram, train or bike (also to work or school), or to another town

answer.title: jechać
answer.text: One trip with a vehicle: jechać (jadę, jedziesz, jadą). The vehicle is in the instrumental: autobusem, pociągiem.

examples.pl: Kiedy jechałam do pracy, zadzwoniła mama.
examples.en: While I was on my way to work, Mum called.

options.label: By plane

answer.title: lecieć
answer.text: One flight: lecieć (lecę, lecisz, lecą).

examples.en: The plane is flying to Rome.

options.label: On foot, or to everyday places in town when the sentence names no vehicle

answer.title: chodzić
answer.text: A habit on foot, or walking in general: chodzić (chodzę, chodzisz, chodzą). Also "can walk": Nasz syn już chodzi.

examples.pl: W niedziele lubimy chodzić po parku.
examples.en: On Sundays we like walking around the park.

options.label: By vehicle or bike (also to work or school), or to other towns

answer.title: jeździć
answer.text: A habit with a vehicle, or riding in general: jeździć (jeżdżę, jeździsz, jeżdżą). Watch the spelling: jeżdżę.

examples.en: I cycle to work every day.

options.label: By plane, or flying in general

answer.title: latać
answer.text: Flying as a habit or an activity: latać (latam, latasz, latają).

examples.pl: Moja siostra często lata do Londynu.
examples.en: My sister often flies to London.

done.question: How did or will you travel?

options.label: On foot, or to an everyday place in town when no vehicle is named

answer.title: pójść
answer.text: One finished trip on foot: pójść. Past poszedł / poszła, future pójdę. For a plan both work: Jutro idę / pójdę. A past trip there and back: Wczoraj byłem w kinie.

examples.en: I'll go to the doctor's tomorrow.

options.label: By vehicle (also to work or school), or to another town or country

answer.title: pojechać
answer.text: One finished trip with a vehicle: pojechać. Past pojechał / pojechała, future pojadę. For a plan both work: Jutro jadę / pojadę.

examples.pl: W zeszłym roku pojechaliśmy do Włoch.
examples.en: Last year we went to Italy.
In August we'll go to Gdańsk.

options.label: By plane

answer.title: polecieć
answer.text: One finished flight: polecieć. Past poleciał / poleciała, future polecę.

examples.en: On Saturday we'll fly to Paris.

trees.title: Imperfective or perfective?
trees.intro: Most verbs come in pairs: robić / zrobić, kupować / kupić. Answer the questions about your sentence to choose the verb of the pair. (być, mieć, znać, wiedzieć have no perfective partner.)

options.label: Now, at the moment of speaking, or as a present habit

answer.title: Imperfective (robić)
answer.text: Only imperfective verbs have a present tense. A perfective verb in a present form means the future: zrobię = I'll do.

examples.en: I read the paper every day.

options.label: In the past or in the future
It is a command or a request

kind.question: What does the sentence say about the action?

options.label: One finished action with a result (już, w końcu), or one event in a chain of events

answer.title: Perfective (zrobić)
answer.text: One result, or one step after another: perfective. Past napisałam; future napiszę, with no będę.

examples.pl: Wstałem, zjadłem śniadanie i poszedłem do pracy.
examples.en: I got up, ate breakfast and went to work.

options.label: A habit or a repeated action (codziennie, często, zawsze, zwykle)

answer.title: Imperfective (robić)
answer.text: Repeated actions take the imperfective. Future: będę + infinitive.

examples.en: From Monday I'm going to run every day.

options.label: How long, the process ("was doing", "will be doing": cały dzień, długo), or just the activity with no result in view (Co robiłeś wczoraj? — Oglądałem telewizję.)

answer.title: Imperfective (robić)
answer.text: Duration and process take the imperfective. Never będę + a perfective verb.

examples.en: Tomorrow I'll be working at home.

options.label: The background while something else happened

answer.title: Imperfective (robić)
answer.text: The background is imperfective; the event that cuts in is perfective.

examples.en: While I was reading, the phone rang.

command.question: What kind of command is it?

options.label: Do it once (a request with a result)

answer.title: Perfective (zrobić)
answer.text: One request, one result: usually the perfective imperative.

options.label: Do it regularly, or keep doing it

answer.title: Imperfective (robić)
answer.text: Something regular or ongoing: the imperfective imperative.

options.label: Don't do it

answer.title: Imperfective (robić)
answer.text: "Don't" almost always takes the imperfective, and the object goes into the genitive.
